name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
description: Adobe Commerce (Magento) is an extensible B2B/B2C commerce platform with REST and GraphQL web APIs.
auth_notes: Token auth from username and password, OAuth for third-party integrations, session cookies for widgets; SaaS uses IMS OAuth server-to-server.
gate_detail: Requires an Adobe Commerce instance where an admin registers an integration, or an Adobe Developer Console project for SaaS. Pricing and signup terms not stated.
api_scope: REST web APIs for PaaS and SaaS, GraphQL endpoint, event-driven integrations, App Builder and aio CLI tooling.
mcp_notes: Commerce development MCPs and skills for coding agents, installed with aio CLI; dev tooling rather than store API.
blocker_detail: Needs a merchant-administered Adobe Commerce instance or Adobe Developer Console org; no self-serve signup described.

evidence.quote: Third-party applications use OAuth-based authentication to access the web APIs.
The token service returns a unique authentication token in exchange for a username and password for an admin or customer account.
Merchants authorize extensions and applications to access or update store data.
The REST API documentation describes the REST APIs that are available in Adobe Commerce (PaaS) and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS).
you can use the Commerce development MCPs and skills to convert existing Adobe Commerce PHP extensions to Adobe Developer App Builder applications.
To prove your identity, specify this token in the Authorization request header on web API calls.
You must register a web service on Admin.
Support for GraphQL , REST (Representational State Transfer) and SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol).
The system does not currently support webhooks.

issues: Cost and signup path for an instance not stated.
MCP is development tooling, not a hosted data server.

searches.query: Magento (Adobe Commerce) API credentials pricing plan required developer access

auth.reason: Source states OAuth 1.0a for third-party apps, which is not OAuth2; no allowed value fits exactly, so Other.

self_serve.reason: Only an admin setup step is described; no source states approval, trial, paid or free access terms.

mcp_status.reason: Adobe's own developer docs publish Commerce development MCPs, including a commerce-extensibility MCP server.
